 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, challenging the impugned judgment and award dated March 28, 2018, passed in MVC No. 7081/2016 by the learned XXI Additional Small Causes Judge and Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH-23).
2.

entities.text: Additional Small Causes Judge and Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH-23)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking just and proper compensation for the death of M.P. Manoj Kumar, who succumbed to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
The Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.7,98,000/- with interest at 6% per annum.
Being dissatisfied with this award, the claimant has appealed for an enhancement of the compensation.
3. The learned counsel for the parties have been heard.

4. It is undisputed that the son of the claimant-appellant died in a road traffic accident on March 21,
2016, and was 32 years old at the time of the accident.

In the absence of proof of income, the notional income of the deceased is to be taken at Rs.9,500/-
NC: 2024:KHC:21586 per month, as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka Legal Aid Services Authority.
Adding 40% towards the loss of future prospects (9,500 x 40% = 3,800/-), and deducting 50% towards personal expenses, the income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.6,650/- per month.
By applying a multiplier of 16, the compensation towards loss of dependency amounts to Rs.12,76,800/- (6,650 x 12 x 16).
5. The compensation awarded towards loss of consortium is deemed to be on the lower side.
The claimant- appellant is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- for loss of consortium and Rs.30,000/- for loss of estate and funeral expenses.
In total, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.13,46,800/- as opposed to the Rs.7,98,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: The claimant-appellant is therefore entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.5,48,800/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of the petition until the date of realization.
7. To this extent, the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
The insurer is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount within three months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
8. Accordingly, the appeal is disposed of.
